smell_elimination.justification: The diff changes only a type annotation on an unrelated helper function (_is_file_like), from te.TypeGuard[t.IO[t.Any]] to bool. This change has no relationship to the interface segregation smell described. None of the problematic methods (validate_constraints, get_diagnostic_info, resolve_value_source) are addressed.

cross_file_coordination.justification: No cross-file changes are present. The calls in core.py (Parameter.process_value, deprecation logic) that depend on the fat interface are not modified. The smell exists across types.py and core.py, but only a trivial annotation change in types.py is made.

structural_soundness.justification: The structural change itself (replacing TypeGuard with bool) is technically reasonable for a file-like check, but it's completely orthogonal to the interface segregation problem. The fat ParamType interface structure remains entirely intact with all three problematic methods still forcing dependencies on subclasses.

code_quality.justification: The annotation change from TypeGuard to bool is a minor simplification that may improve readability slightly (TypeGuard is arguably overkill here), but this is unrelated to fixing the smell. Code quality regarding the interface segregation issue is unchanged.

interface_decomposition.justification: No interface decomposition has occurred. The ParamType base class still contains all three problematic methods (validate_constraints, get_diagnostic_info, resolve_value_source). No interfaces have been split or responsibilities separated.

split_quality.justification: No interface splitting was attempted. All the stub implementations (like Path.validate_constraints) remain. The mandatory base interface is unchanged, still forcing all subclasses to inherit methods they don't need.

interface_segregation_resolution.justification: The three problematic methods remain in the ParamType base interface. Subclasses are still forced to inherit validate_constraints, get_diagnostic_info, and resolve_value_source. The no-op Path.validate_constraints override still exists. The fat interface is completely unaddressed.

concern_separation_and_coupling_reductio.justification: Validation, diagnostics, and value-source tracking remain mixed in the type interface. The coupling between Parameter.process_value and validate_constraints is unchanged. Context metadata pollution persists. No separation of concerns was attempted.

aspect_3_judge.summary: This refactoring does not address the interface segregation smell at all. The single change (a type annotation on an unrelated helper function) has no connection to the fat ParamType interface problem. All three problematic methods remain in the base class, forcing dependencies on subclasses that don't need them, with no decomposition, separation of concerns, or coupling reduction attempted.
